Code Defect: When adding `<script>` or `<link>` tags that load resources from an external CDN (e.g., in `src/docs/index.html`), always include a Subresource Integrity (SRI) `integrity` attribute with the cryptographic hash of the resource, plus a matching `crossorigin` attribute. Loading CDN assets without an integrity check exposes users to supply-chain attacks.

In async rendering loops in diagram-dispatching code (e.g., `mermaid.ts`), do not use `Promise.all` for parallel `render` calls. Diagram database modules (e.g., `flowDb.js`) rely on module-level mutable state, so concurrent renders corrupt each other's output. Sequential `await` is required. This is a known architectural limitation tracked in issue #3577.

When documentation code examples reference mermaid via CDN, always include an explicit version pin. In source files under `packages/mermaid/src/docs/` processed by the `docs.mts` build transform, use the `<MERMAID_VERSION>` placeholder. In files served directly (e.g., standalone HTML in `vdocs/`), hardcode the current major version (e.g., `@9`). Unversioned CDN URLs break archived docs when a new major version is released.

When adding or reviewing code examples in documentation that reference mermaid module file paths, verify filenames are correctly spelled — e.g., the ESM build artifact is `mermaid.esm.mjs`, not `mermaid.ems.mjs`.

When modifying header-generation logic in `packages/mermaid/src/docs.mts`, verify that the relative path in the autogenerated 'DO NOT EDIT' source-file link is derived from the *output* file's directory depth under `docs/`, not from the source file path. Spot-check generated headers for at least one top-level file and one subdirectory file.

Pre-release version identifiers in semver strings must include a dot before the numeric component (e.g., `9.2.1-rc.1`, not `9.2.1-rc1`). Without the dot, identifiers are compared lexicographically, causing `rc10 < rc9`. Verify this format whenever `package.json` version fields are modified.

When refactoring a callback from a function parameter into an optional interface property, verify that at least one concrete implementation actually sets that property before adding a conditional guard in the calling code. If no implementation sets it, remove the branch rather than leaving dead code.

When adding or modifying entries in the redirect map (`packages/mermaid/src/docs/.vitepress/theme/redirect.ts`), verify that every non-empty target path resolves to an actual, content-bearing documentation page; spot-check target URLs in the running dev server before merging.

Use `window.location.replace()` instead of assigning to `window.location.href` when performing client-side redirects, so the source URL is not pushed onto the browser history stack and users can navigate back without being caught in a redirect loop.

In every diagram detector file (`*Detector.ts`), diagram definition file (`*Diagram.ts` / `*Diagram-v*.ts`), diagram loader function, renderer module (`renderer.ts`), and styles module (`styles.ts`), exported constants and functions must carry explicit type annotations using the project's shared types (`DiagramDetector`, `DiagramDefinition`, `DiagramLoader`, `DiagramRenderer`/`DrawDefinition`, `DiagramStylesProvider` from `../../diagram-api/types.js`). Omitting these forfeits TypeScript's structural checking for required fields and breaks consistency with the rest of the codebase.

When reviewing or adding parameterized test cases in diagram-detection tests (e.g., `diagram-orchestration.spec.ts`), verify that each `(input text, expected diagram type)` pair matches the actual detector logic. The mapping from input text to type name (e.g., `flowchart` vs `flowchart-v2`) is non-obvious — cross-check against the detector source code rather than assuming from the diagram keyword.

In a `"type": "module"` package, do not add `"main"` or `"require"` export fields pointing to `.js` files alongside ESM files — Node.js treats all `.js` files in that context as ESM, so `require()` will fail at runtime. If CJS support is needed, use `.cjs` extensions or place CJS files in a subdirectory with its own `{ "type": "commonjs" }` package.json.

When modifying `exports`, `types`, or `main` fields in package.json, verify that type exports are correct for all relevant `moduleResolution` modes using https://arethetypeswrong.github.io before merging, to catch CJS/ESM TypeScript incompatibilities (e.g., broken types under `moduleResolution: node16`).

When removing or renaming files in the `dist/` directory of a published npm package, check whether those paths are referenced by CDN URLs. `unpkg.com` returns a 404 for missing files (unlike jsdelivr, which falls back to older versions), permanently breaking downstream `<script src>` CDN links. The `dist/mermaid.min.js` filename in particular has a large number of CDN dependents and must be treated as a stable public artifact.

When bumping the `packageManager` version in `package.json` (this project uses pnpm), delete the lockfile (`pnpm-lock.yaml`) entirely and regenerate it by running the new package manager's install command from scratch. Simply committing a manually edited lockfile does not guarantee stale entries from the prior version are fully removed.

When implementing runtime detection of a browser built-in API (e.g., `if (Intl.Segmenter)`), add unit tests that stub the API as `undefined` via `vi.stubGlobal` to exercise the fallback code path. In the test description or a comment, note which browser lacks support and link to the relevant bug report or spec discussion.

Mermaid diagram syntax changes must not break previously-valid diagram source. When modifying grammar productions (e.g., in `flow.jison`): (1) add regression tests for edge cases that were previously valid (e.g., trailing backslash in quoted labels, special characters at string boundaries), (2) when widening a non-terminal (e.g., replacing `alphaNum` with `idString`), add tests confirming newly-accepted forms and asserting previously-rejected forms still fail, (3) for reserved-keyword changes in identifiers, test keywords as prefixes, suffixes, and infixes with each permitted punctuation separator. When modifying a regex controlling accepted syntax modifier/classifier characters (e.g., in `classTypes.ts`), verify the accepted character set against the official documentation and explicitly assess whether removing previously-accepted characters constitutes a breaking change. When a conflict arises between a new feature and backward compatibility, the old behavior must be preserved.

In diagram modules (especially those marked `-beta`), prefer `log.warn` over throwing exceptions when detecting input that violates a soft constraint but was previously silently tolerated, to avoid introducing breaking changes for existing diagrams that relied on the permissive behavior. Reserve `throw` for hard errors that prevent meaningful rendering.

When a TypeScript function accepts a destructured config/options parameter that callers may partially specify, assign defaults at the property level (e.g., `{ depth = 2, clobber = false }`) and mark those properties optional in the type. A whole-object default (`= {}`) only applies when the argument is entirely omitted — it does not merge missing fields from a partially-provided object. Do not combine destructuring defaults with `Object.assign` for the same parameter; choose one approach, preferring destructuring defaults.

In development demo files (e.g., under `demos/`) and client-side event-driven code (EventSource, WebSocket, etc.), ensure error event handlers explicitly log the error to the console rather than silently ignoring it, so failures are visible during development.

When configuring file-watcher ignore patterns (e.g., chokidar's `ignored` option), verify that patterns intended to exclude directories like `node_modules` match at all nesting levels (e.g., use `**/node_modules/**` glob syntax), not only at the root of the watched tree.

When defining TypeScript interfaces for diagram data objects (e.g., in `packages/mermaid/src/diagrams/common/commonTypes.ts`), audit actual call sites to determine which fields are genuinely optional before adding `?`. Do not mark all fields optional just to suppress TypeScript errors — only fields that are truly nullable or omittable at every call site should carry `?`; fields that are always required must remain non-optional to preserve type-safety guarantees.

When a JS-to-TS conversion includes any change that could alter runtime behavior (even a small bug fix such as correcting `x !== 'undefined'` to `x !== undefined`), run the project's end-to-end tests (`pnpm run e2e`) against the branch, comparing outputs against a `develop` baseline, before merging — to confirm that no diagram rendering outputs change unexpectedly.

When measuring elapsed or wall-clock duration (e.g., timing build steps or async operations), prefer `console.time()`/`console.timeEnd()` or `performance.now()` over `Date.now()`. `Date.now()` reflects the system wall clock and is not monotonic, making it unsuitable for measuring time intervals.

`packages/mermaid/src/config.type.ts` is auto-generated from `packages/mermaid/src/schemas/config.schema.yaml` and must not be modified manually. New diagram configuration types must be added to the YAML schema file and the TypeScript file regenerated via the project's build script.

New diagram jison grammars must not include `%%{...}%%` directive parsing logic; directives are pre-processed by the framework before any diagram-specific grammar runs, making diagram-level directive rules redundant and potentially conflicting.

Grammar rules for bracket-delimited lists (e.g., `[ item, item, ... ]`) should use explicit bracket terminals and a dedicated non-terminal for the list body; avoid recursive rules that allow unbalanced constructions such as `[ 10 [ 20 ]`.

In jison lexers, use `pushState` instead of `begin` for delimiter nesting, and ensure every `pushState` on an opening delimiter has a matching `popState` on the corresponding closing delimiter; avoid creating unnecessary intermediate states when the state stack already manages nesting. Using `begin` replaces (rather than pushes) the current state, which can corrupt the state stack.
In jison lexer rules, list closing delimiter tokens (e.g., `"]"`) before content-matching patterns within the same lexer state so they take higher matching priority and cannot be consumed as content.

When `accTitle` and `accDescr` accessibility tokens appear in a jison grammar (even if copied from another diagram), they must be fully implemented with corresponding grammar actions and DB calls; leaving them as stubs breaks screen-reader accessibility for the diagram.

When copying regex patterns into a new jison grammar from an existing diagram, review each pattern for correctness in the new context; copied patterns (e.g., for directive comment detection or negative lookaheads) may only partially work and should be understood before being retained.

DOM elements created for text dimension measurement (e.g., hidden `<text>` nodes appended to SVG) must be removed after use to avoid polluting the document. Prefer existing project utilities such as `computeWidthOfText` or `computeDimensionOfText` in `packages/mermaid/src/rendering-util/createText.ts` that already handle cleanup. Use the SVG-based approach (not canvas) so the correct font family, size, and style context is applied; reusable rendering helpers belong in `packages/mermaid/src/rendering-util/`, not inlined in individual diagram renderers.

When copying or merging nested config or theme objects, use the project's `cleanAndMerge` or `assignWithDepth` utilities rather than shallow spread operators (`{ ...obj }`) or raw `structuredClone`. Shallow spread does not deep-copy nested objects and can produce silent shared-reference mutations. Prefer `assignWithDepth` over `structuredClone` for config objects, as `structuredClone` is not universally supported across all target browser environments.

Diagram detector regexes must require the complete diagram keyword including any suffix as declared in the grammar (e.g., `/^\s*xychart-beta/` for a diagram declared as `xychart-beta`); omitting the suffix silently pre-empts the project's explicit beta-to-stable graduation process. Detector regexes should also be case-sensitive, consistent with other diagram detectors in the project.

When a class method's output depends on other mutable state (e.g., `setAxisPosition` affects the coordinate range), updating that state should automatically trigger any dependent recalculation inside the same method; callers should not be required to invoke methods in a specific order to get correct results.

When reviewing typo-fix changes, check whether any corrected string literal is part of the library's externally observable API — for example, error message text that is thrown or returned to callers who may be matching it programmatically. Changing such strings is a breaking change; flag it for rejection or deferral to the next major release rather than treating it as a safe cosmetic fix.

Diagram text preprocessing must be applied exactly once at the appropriate layer. Input-normalization steps shared across all code paths (e.g., comment stripping, frontmatter extraction via `preprocessDiagram`) belong at the public API boundary layer (`mermaidAPI.ts`), not inside lower-level modules like `Diagram.ts` that are invoked from multiple paths. Diagram-specific transformations (e.g., entity encoding) belong in the `Diagram` class constructor. Centralizing each transformation at the correct layer prevents double-processing bugs.

Avoid polynomial (potentially catastrophic-backtracking) regular expressions on uncontrolled user input. Patterns that combine multiple greedy quantifiers with overlapping character classes — such as `style.*:\S*#.*;` — can degrade to exponential time on crafted inputs, creating a ReDoS vulnerability. Use more precise, non-backtracking patterns (e.g., negated character classes or possessive quantifiers) when processing diagram text and node label strings (including HTML tag patterns like `` in `rendering-util/rendering-elements/shapes/util.js`), and flag any such patterns for a security review.

When configuring the Shiki syntax-highlighting theme in the VitePress config (`packages/mermaid/src/docs/.vitepress/config.ts`), always use the dual-mode object form `{ light: '<light-theme>', dark: '<dark-theme>' }` instead of a single theme string. A single string will break code-block highlighting in whichever color mode it was not chosen for, since the site supports both light and dark modes.

When using DOMPurify hooks in `common.ts` `removeScript()`, register *all* hooks—including `afterSanitizeAttributes`—before calling `DOMPurify.sanitize()`, not after; and remove each hook afterward with `DOMPurify.removeHook()` to prevent hooks from accumulating across repeated calls.

When re-applying an HTML attribute that DOMPurify strips (e.g., `target` on `<a>` elements), restore the attribute's exact original value rather than substituting a hardcoded default; only add security-hardening companion attributes (e.g., `rel="noopener noreferrer"`) for the specific values that require them (e.g., `target="_blank"`).

Before adding calls to DOMPurify hook methods such as `addHook` in `common.ts`, verify that those methods are available in the Jest test environment; if DOMPurify is mocked or only partially shimmed in tests, extend the mock (or use a real DOM environment like jsdom) so that the full hook API is exercisable.

When simplifying DOM positioning arithmetic that mixes DOMRect properties (e.g., `rect.top`, `rect.bottom`), scroll offsets (`window.scrollY`, `document.body.scrollTop`), and numeric constants, verify that the simplified expression is mathematically equivalent under all scroll states and document the reasoning — either in an inline comment or the PR description — so reviewers can confirm correctness.

In `packages/mermaid/src/schemas/config.schema.yaml`, every property definition must include an explicit `type` field and a `default` value — do not rely on type inference from the `default` value, and do not omit defaults. Use `type: number` for properties that can accept floating-point values; use `type: integer` only when the property semantically requires a whole number (e.g., a count), and add a `minimum` constraint for properties that must be non-negative.

When converting an implicit runtime crash (e.g., a TypeError from an out-of-bounds access) into an explicit `throw new Error(...)`, verify that the test suite includes a test asserting the specific error is thrown — not just that no crash occurs.

In Jest/Vitest tests, `.toThrow()` must be chained on the `expect()` call itself, not placed inside the callback. The correct pattern is `expect(() => fn()).toThrow(message)`. Placing `.toThrow()` inside the arrow (e.g., `expect(() => fn().toThrow(message))`) silently turns the assertion into a no-op. Flag any test where `.toThrow()` appears inside the `expect(() => ...)` callback.

When a regex captures characters that feed into a downstream handler (e.g., a switch or conditional block), verify every character the updated regex can match is actually handled downstream. Characters accepted by the regex but absent from the downstream handler silently do nothing; their presence often signals an accidental addition whose removal must be explicitly confirmed as safe.

When a refactor renames parameters, check whether any logic referencing those parameters by position or index also needs updating. A parameter rename that silently changes which entity's property (e.g., `.branch`) is used in a comparison is a semantic change, not a cosmetic one, and must be explicitly flagged and justified in the PR.

Every new or modified conditional branch in rendering logic (e.g., arrow-routing, colour-selection in `gitGraphRenderer.js`) must be covered by at least one e2e or snapshot test. When adding a rendering fix or new behavior to demo files (e.g., `demos/flowchart.html`), also add a corresponding `imgSnapshotTest` in the relevant Cypress spec. Verify that each predicate's true-returning path is actually reachable in practice and flag any branch without test coverage.

When modifying the `build:types` script (currently driven by `.build/types.ts`), ensure TypeScript declaration generation runs in strict package-dependency order — `parser` first, then `mermaid`, then remaining packages — because each downstream package's compilation depends on the previous stage's emitted `.d.ts` files. Parallel strategies such as `pnpm --recursive exec tsc --emitDeclarationOnly` break this ordering and will produce type errors.

In external diagram/plugin packages (e.g., `mermaid-flowchart-elk`, `mermaid-zenuml`) and new monorepo packages intended to be consumed alongside an existing package (e.g., `@mermaid-js/examples`), declare `mermaid` (or the relevant core package) as a `peerDependency` using the `workspace:^` protocol (e.g., `"mermaid": "workspace:^"`). This ensures `pnpm publish` automatically resolves to the correct released version, prevents breaking downstream consumers when mermaid introduces breaking changes, and lets package managers warn users about incompatible version combinations. Do not place such dependencies in `devDependencies`.

When interpolating user-provided or parser-derived strings into SVG attribute values that use `url(...)` syntax (e.g., marker-start, marker-end), validate the input against an explicit allowlist (see `arrowTypesMap` in `dagre-wrapper/edgeMarker.ts`) and return early without calling `.attr()` for any unrecognized value. Do not construct the attribute string from an unvalidated input — a value containing `)` or a full URL can corrupt the `url(...)` syntax or inject a malicious reference.

When writing tests for functions that accept arbitrary strings and produce SVG or HTML attribute values, include at least one test case with a syntactically invalid input and one with a potentially malicious string (e.g., containing `)`, embedded URLs, or CSS injection attempts) to verify that the allowlist/sanitization check rejects them and leaves the element's attributes unchanged.

When combining optional boolean/numeric config flags from multiple sources, use the nullish coalescing operator `??` instead of `||` so that intentional `false` or `0` values are not silently overridden. `||` treats `0`, `false`, and `""` as falsy and falls back, while `??` only falls back on `null` or `undefined`.

When setting the `viewBox` attribute on an SVG element, use the native DOM API (`elem.setAttribute("viewBox", ...)`) rather than a d3 `.attr()` call. `viewBox` is case-sensitive in SVG; d3 or certain DOM wrappers may lowercase it to `viewbox`, which silently breaks SVG rendering.

Rendering changes that affect SVG output attributes (e.g., `viewBox`, `width`, `style`) must be accompanied by integration tests (e.g., in `cypress/integration/rendering/`) that assert the expected attribute values on the rendered SVG element.

Verify that every call site matches the target function's parameter list exactly; remove extra arguments that have no corresponding parameter in the function signature. Extra arguments are silently ignored at runtime but indicate a logic error or stale call site.

Helper functions that search for a value and may come up empty should return `undefined` (not an empty string or other falsy sentinel) when no match exists. Callers must guard against the `undefined` return before using the result as a key into dependent data structures (e.g., `commitPos`).

Variables derived from a base value (e.g., `posWithOffset = pos + layoutOffset`) must be computed *after* all mutations to that base value within the same scope. Declaring derived variables before a block that modifies the base produces stale, incorrect values.

In Langium grammar files, define the `INT` terminal as `/0|[1-9][0-9]*/` to disallow leading zeros (e.g., `00` would otherwise parse as a valid integer, which TypeScript and JavaScript do not accept as a numeric literal).

When registering a new diagram's config entry in `defaultConfig.ts`, explicitly set `useMaxWidth: true` to remain consistent with all other diagrams (only `gitGraph` intentionally deviates from this default).

When defining a diagram-specific `*DB` interface that extends `DiagramDBBase`, explicitly re-declare any optional `DiagramDB` fields the diagram provides (e.g., `getDiagramTitle`, `setAccTitle`, `getAccDescription`) to make them required rather than relying on the inherited optional signature, so TypeScript enforces their implementation.

In diagram renderers, call `configureSvgSize(svg, height, width, config.useMaxWidth)` before setting the SVG `viewBox` attribute, following the established pattern in `pieRenderer.ts`. This ensures the SVG element dimensions and viewBox are configured in the correct order.

For new diagram types, prefer the class-based DB architecture where mutable state is managed as class instance properties with explicit access modifiers (e.g., `private nodes: Node[] = []`); the class itself is the state container, and `ImperativeState` is not needed. For existing functional-export DB modules, do not use bare module-level mutable variables (`let x = 0`); use the project's `ImperativeState` utility (from `packages/mermaid/src/utils/imperativeState.ts`) for all mutable diagram-module state. Initialize state — including config-derived values such as `mainBranchName` and `mainBranchOrder` — inside the factory callback so values are re-read from `getConfig()` and reset correctly between diagrams.

Do not wrap functions in `try...catch` unless they can actually throw; also remove `any` casts that exist only to suppress TypeScript errors caused by incorrect type annotations elsewhere — fix the annotations instead.

Verify that all Mermaid diagram strings used as fixtures in Cypress and unit tests are syntactically valid (e.g., no unclosed string literals, correct token separation such as closing parentheses before `:N` width specifiers) to prevent false test failures.

SVG/D3 attribute values can legally be either strings or numbers. Ensure that diagram node and shape property type definitions use an appropriate `string | number` union rather than narrowing to only `number` when string values are also valid, to avoid incorrect type errors at call sites.

When auto-computing axis bounds for charts with multiple or stacked datasets (e.g., xychart), the lower bound must include the appropriate baseline (typically 0), not just the raw minimum of individual data values. For stacked bars, the upper bound must be the largest per-column sum — i.e., for each x-position, sum the values of all datasets at that position, then take the max across positions. Using the global max of individual values or a total sum across all positions will produce an incorrect axis ceiling. Audit the min/max derivation logic in the chart's DB module (e.g., `xychartDb.ts`).

In Langium `runCustomConverter` implementations for diagram `ValueConverter` classes, strip only the necessary wrapper characters from matched tokens (e.g., remove surrounding quotes from a label terminal) and trim the ends of the resulting string. Do not collapse or otherwise normalize internal whitespace in user-provided values, as doing so silently alters user intent.

When a new demo block is created by copying an existing one, update ALL content-specific fields to match the new demo's subject matter — including the `accTitle` and `accDescr` accessibility attributes — not just the visible `title`. Stale accessibility metadata left over from the copied block is misleading and functionally incorrect.

In Langium diagram grammars where `NEWLINE` tokens are semantically significant, do not use `\s+` as a hidden terminal (it would subsume NEWLINE and break rule matching). Define the `EOL` fragment as `NEWLINE+ | EOF` and use it to delimit block-level rules. Require `NEWLINE+` between the diagram keyword and any content, and between block-level rules, so that multiple blocks cannot appear on the same line.

When writing regular expressions, avoid overly broad character class ranges such as `[A-z]`, which inadvertently include non-alphabetic ASCII characters (e.g., `[`, `\`, `]`, `^`, `_`, `` ` ``); use explicit, tightly scoped ranges such as `[A-Za-z]` or `[A-Z]` and `[a-z]` separately instead.

In documentation source files under `packages/mermaid/src/docs/`, version-gated feature headings must use the placeholder `(v<MERMAID_RELEASE_VERSION>+)` rather than a hardcoded version number — this placeholder is automatically substituted with the actual release version by the docs build pipeline that publishes content to the `docs/` directory.

Do not silently correct apparent typos in jison `%options` directives. A misspelled option name is effectively a no-op, but changing it to the correct spelling can inadvertently enable a feature (some jison options are enabled by default in certain implementations). Either delete the questionable option entirely, or suppress the spell-check warning with a `// cspell: disable-line` comment and leave the original text unchanged, noting why it must stay misspelled.

When modifying a shared theme variable default in any of the theme files (`theme-base.js`, `theme-default.js`, `theme-dark.js`, `theme-forest.js`, `theme-neutral.js`), verify the rendered appearance across all five built-in themes (default, neutral, dark, forest, base) before requesting review, since a single variable change can affect each theme differently.

When a keyboard shortcut is displayed in the UI (e.g., hint text like 'Ctrl + Enter'), verify that the corresponding event handler actually fires on all advertised platforms before merging. For example, the Vue `@keydown.meta.enter` modifier only triggers for the Meta key (Cmd on macOS) and does NOT cover Ctrl on Windows/Linux — if Ctrl+Enter is also advertised, a separate `@keydown.ctrl.enter` binding is required. Manually test the shortcut on at least one non-Mac platform (or a Ctrl-only context) to confirm it works.

New diagram features that affect parsing, data model, and visual output must have test coverage at all three layers: DB-layer unit tests (e.g., `ganttDb.spec.ts`), parser-level unit tests (e.g., `gantt.spec.js`), and end-to-end rendering/visual snapshot tests (e.g., `cypress/integration/rendering/gantt.spec.js`). Tests that only exercise internal DB functions in isolation are insufficient on their own.

When introducing a new config flag that gates existing behavior (e.g., suppressing error rendering): (a) audit the entire function or module for every code path where that behavior occurs and apply the gate consistently — not just the first occurrence; (b) ensure that side-effects in the original code — especially `throw` statements — are preserved in the default (flag-off) branch, so the pre-existing default behavior is never silently changed.

In Cypress E2E tests that assert on collections of SVG elements (e.g., `.find('svg').should(...)`), add per-element visibility checks (e.g., `expect(cy.$$(svg)).to.be.visible`) alongside length and content assertions to prevent race conditions where elements are present in the DOM but not yet fully rendered.

When propagating parent graph properties to subgraph configurations in `dagre-wrapper` (e.g., `node.graph.setGraph` before a `recursiveRender` call), explicitly destructure and copy only the specific properties you intend to override (e.g., `ranksep`, `nodesep`) rather than spreading the full parent graph config, which silently overwrites subgraph-specific layout values (such as `marginy`).

In `gitGraphRenderer.js`, when computing a commit's rendered position for any orientation, derive it from the closest parent's stored position (`commitPos[closestParent]`), not from the current commit's pre-computed `commitPos[key]`. Collapse orientation branches that share the same axis (e.g., `TB` and `BT`) into a single `dir === 'TB' || dir === 'BT'` condition to prevent subtle divergence bugs.

Never rename or modify the title strings of existing test cases in snapshot-based or image-comparison test suites (e.g., Cypress `imgSnapshotTest`); test titles are used to derive snapshot file names, so renaming orphans prior baselines and breaks comparisons.

When validating user-provided values in diagram parsers or DB layers (e.g., style property names, color formats), throw an explicit, descriptive error (e.g., a custom `Error` subclass) rather than silently ignoring or only logging a warning.

New parsing or validation utility functions must have dedicated unit tests covering: valid input with all supported parameters, empty/missing input, unsupported property names, and each distinct category of invalid value format (e.g., bad hex code, non-numeric value, missing unit suffix).

When building rendered data objects from raw input, apply fallback-to-theme-default patterns (e.g., `point.property ?? themeDefault`) consistently for all overridable style properties; do not hardcode defaults for some while using the pattern for others.

Expected error message strings in unit tests must exactly match the messages produced by the source code's error constructors; cross-check character-for-character against actual constructor arguments to avoid false-passing tests.

When flattening a nested type across the codebase (e.g., `{ actor: string }` → `string`), verify the refactor is applied at every call site. Double-dereference patterns (e.g., `param.actor.actor`) signal that the upstream data producer (e.g., a jison grammar rule) still emits the old shape and must be corrected at the source, not patched around in downstream consumers.

When accessing values from a `Map` with `.get()`, do not use the TypeScript `!` non-null assertion on the result. In production code, cache the `.get()` result in a named local variable and guard against `undefined` before use (e.g., `const node = map.get(id); if (node === undefined) { ... }`). In test assertions, prefer optional chaining (`?.`) for safe property access on `.get()` results.

When checking whether an optional string or numeric parameter was provided, use strict equality (`=== undefined` or `!== undefined`) rather than a truthy/falsy check (`if (text)`). A falsy check incorrectly treats empty string `''` and `0` (including valid numeric enum values like `commitType.NORMAL`) as absent, which changes behavior whenever those are semantically valid values.

When declaring a mutable variable that will later be assigned a structured value, always include an explicit type annotation (e.g., `let msgModel: MessageModel | null = null`). Without it, TypeScript infers the type from the initializer (e.g., `null`), causing all subsequent property accesses to resolve to `never` and hiding real type errors from the compiler.

In `rendering-util/rendering-elements/` modules (e.g., `edges.js`, `createLabel.js`), all user-supplied string values embedded into SVG or HTML output must be fully escaped or sanitized before insertion. Backslash characters must be escaped to prevent incomplete string encoding, and label content must never be inserted into HTML via direct concatenation — use proper escaping or the project's sanitization utilities to prevent XSS vulnerabilities.

Configuration properties with a fixed set of valid values (such as `look` or edge pattern types) must be typed with explicit, exhaustive union types (e.g., `'classic' | 'handDrawn'`) rather than a generic `string`. Audit all variants to ensure none are omitted — for example, `'dotted'` must be included alongside `'solid'` in edge pattern union types.

In the markdown-to-rendered-text processing pipeline (`handle-markdown-text.ts`), each token handler should emit only the content semantically required by that token type; do not silently inject extra whitespace characters (`' '` or ` `) for tokens that do not produce whitespace, as this corrupts node label text.
In `switch` statements, the `default` case must always call `log.error(...)` or throw an error; never silently skip unhandled cases.

When adding or updating GitHub Actions workflow steps, pin every `uses:` reference — both GitHub-owned actions and third-party actions — by full commit SHA (e.g., `uses: actions/checkout@<full-sha>`). Add an inline comment with the human-readable version (e.g., `# v4.1.7`) for readability. This satisfies OpenSSF Scorecard's pinned-dependencies requirement; Dependabot will keep the hashes up to date automatically.

GitHub Actions workflow files must include a top-level `permissions:` block that restricts the `GITHUB_TOKEN` to the minimum required scopes (e.g., `contents: read`). Omitting this block grants the token broad default access. Scrutinize any `write` permission granted at the job or workflow level (e.g., `contents: write`, `pull-requests: write`). Confirm the permission is the minimum required for the specific actions in that job, verify it cannot be replaced with a finer-grained or read-only alternative, and ensure an inline comment explains why the elevated permission is necessary.

When a test needs to assert that a specific function (e.g., a logger method) was called with particular arguments, write the test in a Vitest unit-test file using `vi.spyOn` and `expect(spy).toHaveBeenCalledWith(...)` rather than in a Cypress integration test using `cy.log`. `cy.log` only emits a message to the Cypress runner UI and makes no assertion about production code behavior.

When a `package.json` already declares `types` paths inside the `exports` field, do not also add a redundant top-level `"types"` field pointing to a different path in `dist/`. The top-level field creates conflicting type resolution and unnecessarily locks the `dist/` folder structure into the public API surface.

In new `packages/*/tsconfig.json` files, use an explicit `"module": "Node16"` (or `"Node18"`) rather than `"module": "NodeNext"`. TypeScript 5.8+ changed the semantics of `NodeNext`, so pinning to an explicit node version avoids unexpected behaviour changes when TypeScript is upgraded.

Do not assign imported functions to class members using arrow-function field syntax (e.g., `public setAccTitle = setAccTitle`). Older Safari versions have known compatibility issues with certain class field initializer expressions; use class methods that delegate to the imported function instead.
Maintainability and Readability: When only values are needed from an object, use `Object.values()` instead of `Object.entries()`. Using `Object.entries()` without destructuring the `[key, value]` pair means accessing named properties (e.g., `element.branch`) on the array pair returns `undefined`. Even when destructuring, discarding the key triggers `no-unused-vars` lint warnings.

When adding ESLint `overrides` in `.eslintrc.json` to suppress rules for test/spec files (e.g., `*.spec.{ts,js}`, `cypress/**`, `docs/**` globs), prefer setting rules to `"warn"` rather than `"off"` so newly introduced violations still appear in PR diffs; only use `"off"` when accumulated warning count is large enough to obscure real errors.

CI status badges in README files (`README.md`, `README.zh-CN.md`, `docs/README.md`, and other variants) must link to the currently active CI system (GitHub Actions). When updating any one README, check that all sibling README variants receive the same badge update.

Variables in `packages/mermaid/src/docs.mts` that hold a specific semver component must be named to reflect which component they contain (e.g., `MERMAID_MAJOR_VERSION` for just the major version, not a generic `mermaidVersion`).

When deprecating or removing public-facing config options, API methods, or package exports, document the change in the CHANGELOG or release notes — not only via in-code deprecation warnings — so existing consumers have clear migration guidance.

When a feature, config key, or code path is removed, replaced, or refactored, audit all related JSDoc blocks, inline comments, and log messages and remove or update any references to the old feature or prior logic; stale documentation and misleading log messages confuse future contributors.

When adding routing or navigation behavior inside the VitePress theme's `enhanceApp` hook (`packages/mermaid/src/docs/.vitepress/theme/index.ts`), prefer using VitePress's official router API (e.g., the `router` object from the `ctx` argument) over directly patching router lifecycle callbacks.

When adding non-obvious logic, workarounds, or hacks in build configuration files or plugin utilities (e.g., a dynamically constructed RegExp in `.vite/build.ts`, a workaround for an upstream bug), include inline comments that (1) explain in plain language what the code does and why the workaround is necessary, (2) attribute any external pattern or source it was adapted from (e.g., `// Adapted from the RegEx used by rollup-plugin-node`), and (3) link to the relevant issue, PR discussion, or upstream bug report so future maintainers can revisit it.

When a change involves both a mechanical file-format migration (e.g., converting a config from JSON to CJS/ESM, renaming files, restructuring without behavior changes) and substantive content changes, split them into separate commits so reviewers can clearly identify what actually changed in each step.

When reorganizing README layout (e.g., adding a centered logo/header), adopt a consistent strategy for badge placement rather than splitting badges across header and body without an explicit reason. Ensure quick-access navigation links (CDN, docs, contribution guide) remain visible and prominent; if relocated, they must reappear somewhere equally discoverable.

Before including links to project files (changelogs, migration guides, other docs) in prominent README sections, verify that the target files are actively maintained and up to date. Remove or replace links to stale or abandoned files to avoid misleading users.

Exported functions whose behavior depends on non-obvious constraints — such as argument ordering (e.g., `registerLazyLoadedDiagrams` where the first matching detector wins) or concurrency semantics (e.g., an execution queue that serializes concurrent calls) — must document these constraints explicitly in a TSDoc `@remarks` block so callers understand the implications.

When a function's signature changes (e.g., parameters added, removed, or retyped; callback-based to promise-based), update all JSDoc for that function: remove or rewrite stale `@param` entries, add `@param` tags for any undocumented parameters, update inline code examples so they compile and run against the new API, and include a `@returns` tag describing the return value. Every parameter in the signature must have a corresponding `@param` tag. Ensure `@returns` type annotations accurately reflect the function's actual return type — a utility documented as returning `string` must always return `string` and never silently return an array or `undefined`. Also flag stale or copy-pasted doc blocks that describe a different function, reference wrong parameter names, or state incorrect behavior.

Auto-generated files (e.g., those emitted by `unplugin-vue-components`, build pipelines, or code-generation scripts such as the contributors JSON) must be added to `.gitignore` and, where appropriate, also to `.prettierignore` and `cSpell.json` `ignorePaths`, so they are excluded from version control, formatting, and spell-checking.

When adding or modifying scripts (e.g., under `scripts/` or `packages/mermaid/src/docs/.vitepress/scripts/`), use `ts-node-esm` — the project's established TypeScript script runner — rather than introducing alternatives like `esno` or `tsx`, to keep script execution consistent.

Prefer Node.js built-in `node:fs/promises` APIs over third-party filesystem utilities (such as `fs-extra`) when they offer equivalent functionality; for example, use `mkdir(path, { recursive: true })` instead of `fs-extra`'s `ensureDir` or `mkdir(path).catch(() => {})` — the `recursive: true` option both creates missing intermediate directories and silently handles EEXIST, making intent explicit without broadly suppressing unrelated errors.

All exported functions must have at least a basic TSDoc/JSDoc comment. When refactoring files (e.g., converting .js to .ts), verify that existing JSDoc comments on exported functions have not been accidentally removed in the process.

When calling APIs whose output depends on environment-specific defaults (e.g., `new Intl.Segmenter(undefined, ...)` using the host locale), add a code comment noting that output may vary across environments or default locales, and cite the relevant spec rationale if locale/platform sensitivity is non-obvious.

When defining a function type alias (or callback type) whose return value is a boolean predicate, include a TSDoc comment that explicitly states which boolean value represents the positive/success case (e.g., `/** Returns true if the line fits the constraint */`).

When modifying or creating jison grammars (e.g., `flow.jison` or new diagram grammars), remove any grammar productions, token definitions, token-list rules, and lexer states that are no longer referenced by any other production, and delete corresponding dead helper code in the associated JS files. When creating a new grammar by adapting an existing one, audit and remove all carried-over rules that are not actually used. Verify with a grep or jison linting pass that no symbol is defined but unused. Do not include grammar rules for syntax features that are not yet implemented or supported; track planned features in issues or TODO comments rather than placeholder grammar rules.

When grammar changes affect which escape sequences or special characters are valid inside node or edge labels, update both `packages/mermaid/src/docs/syntax/flowchart.md` and `docs/syntax/flowchart.md` to accurately reflect the current grammar: remove examples that no longer work, do not introduce examples for forms that have not been verified, and keep the two copies consistent with each other.

In `flow.jison`, keep shape-start/shape-end lexer token rules (e.g., `STADIUMSTART`, `SUBROUTINESTART`, `CYLINDERSTART`) decoupled from text-content state management. Handle quoted and unquoted text within the `text` grammar production (or a dedicated `string` production) rather than embedding `pushState`/`popState` calls inside the lexer rules that emit shape-start tokens. Mixing these concerns produces lexer rules whose entry state does not match their intended exit condition.

In sandbox-aware SVG selection utilities (e.g., `rendering-util/selectSvgElement.ts`), scope intermediate variables like `sandboxElement` and `doc` inside the `if (securityLevel === 'sandbox')` branch rather than hoisting them to the outer scope. When designing such utilities, evaluate whether callers genuinely need the intermediate `Document` or root node — if a renderer misuses `doc` for operations that should target the SVG element, fix the renderer rather than expanding the utility's return type.

Retain a `log.debug(...)` call at the top of diagram renderer `draw` functions even when the function body is not wrapped in a try/catch; it serves as a diagnostic breadcrumb confirming that rendering was entered and helps narrow down where a silent failure occurred.

When exporting a diagram definition object from a diagram module, prefer `export default diagram` over a named `export const diagram` to avoid forcing every import site to alias (e.g., `{ diagram as errorDiagram }`). If a named export is required, name the constant after the diagram (e.g., `export const errorDiagram`) so that imports can consume it without aliasing.

When reviewing `package.json` changes, verify that no deprecated packages have been introduced — including ones that appear to have been auto-added or re-sorted by the package manager (e.g., pnpm) rather than explicitly by the author — and remove any packages flagged as deprecated.

In TypeScript tooling files (e.g., under `.esbuild/`), add explicit type annotations to non-trivial local variables unless their type is already fully and unambiguously constrained by a strongly-typed API; do not rely on implicit inference when the variable's shape is not immediately obvious.

When a JS-to-TS migration reveals a runtime bug (e.g., a comparison against the string `'undefined'` that should instead check the value `undefined`), explicitly call it out in the PR description as a bug fix rather than treating it as an incidental refactoring detail. This helps reviewers understand the behavioral scope of the change and decide whether additional testing or a separate fix PR is warranted.

When adding or updating branch-based Live Editor preview environments, use the `<branch>.git.mermaid.live` subdomain naming convention (not names like `beta.mermaid.live` that imply npm pre-release status). In documentation referencing these previews, use wording that clearly conveys unreleased status (e.g., 'git `develop` branch preview'). Build scripts (e.g., `scripts/editor.bash`) should append the short git commit hash to the mermaid package version so users can identify which commit a preview was built from.

Complex token patterns such as comma-separated lists or structured data should be expressed as non-terminal grammar rules in jison rather than as single large regexes in the lexer; grammar rules produce better parse error messages and are easier to maintain.

When multiple grammar rules (e.g., for different plot types or diagram variants) parse structurally identical data, unify them into a single shared non-terminal; duplication leads to divergent behavior and maintenance overhead.

Default values for new diagram configuration options must be defined in `packages/mermaid/src/schemas/config.schema.yaml` (following the instructions in the file header), not hardcoded in the diagram's DB module; the schema is the single source of truth for defaults.

In functional-export diagram DB modules, all module-level mutable state variables should be grouped at the top of the file (or collected in a single reset object) so that the `clear()` function can reset all state in one place; variables scattered throughout the file are easily missed when adding a reset.

Parser test specifications (`*.jison.spec.ts` files) must include test cases for invalid or malformed inputs that are expected to fail to parse, not only valid happy-path inputs. Also include inputs with varying whitespace around delimiters (commas, colons, tokens) to verify the parser handles whitespace robustly.

Diagram renderers should use the `selectSvgElement` utility from `packages/mermaid/src/rendering-util/selectSvgElement.ts` for obtaining a typed SVG element reference rather than reimplementing that selection inline. Do not reimplement the sandbox/`securityLevel` SVG-selection logic in individual renderer files.
Each section in demo HTML files under `demos/` should have a unique, descriptive heading; avoid repeating the same `<h1>` text for multiple diagram variants in the same file.

When theme variables for a new diagram are structured as a nested object in `themeVariables` (e.g., `themeVariables.xyChart.titleColor`), keep the structure consistent with how other diagrams in the project expose their theme variables to avoid introducing an inconsistent API surface.

Do not add diagram-specific methods (e.g., methods that only certain diagram types expose, such as `getMessages` or `getActors`) to the shared `DiagramDB` interface in `packages/mermaid/src/diagram-api/types.ts`. Diagram-specific DB methods must be typed in the individual diagram's own type definitions, keeping the common interface limited to methods every diagram implementation actually shares.

When extracting cohesive utility functions from a large module (e.g., moving `encodeEntities`/`decodeEntities` out of `mermaidAPI.ts`, or extracting validation helpers like hex-color or pixel-size checks), prefer creating a dedicated, focused module (e.g., `entities.ts`, `styleValidation.ts`) rather than appending them to the general-purpose `utils.ts`. This prevents `utils.ts` from growing into an unrelated grab-bag and makes the utilities easier to discover and test in isolation.

Whenever sanitization behavior in `common.ts` is changed, add unit tests in `common.spec.ts` covering each meaningful input variant: attribute absent, attribute set to a safe/benign value, and attribute set to a risky value that triggers additional hardening.

When generating IDs for diagram edges, use a lexically meaningful template that embeds the source and target node identifiers along with a disambiguating counter—e.g., `id_${edge.id1}_${edge.id2}_${cnt}`—rather than building an opaque ID from a bare counter alone.

When copying a method or code block from a sibling class or module (e.g., a different axis class, a different diagram type), immediately rename all internal identifiers, string literals, and `groupTexts` values to match the new context. Copy-paste identifier mismatches (e.g., `'bottom-axis'` in a top-axis class, or a method name referencing the wrong axis) are a frequent source of silent bugs.
Contributors should not self-resolve review conversation threads after addressing feedback; leave threads open so the reviewer can verify the fix and close them during re-review.

Each `it` test block should cover a single concern; if a test body manually calls `clearMocks()` when a `beforeEach` hook already handles clearing, that is a sign the test should be split into independent `it` blocks.

When documenting a feature that supports multiple modes, orientations, or options, begin the section with an introductory summary listing all supported modes (including syntax keywords and which is the default), then describe the concrete visual behavior of each mode explicitly — state how primary elements flow directionally and how structural elements are arranged — rather than relying on abstract labels alone.

Error messages and diagnostic log messages for invalid-input or constraint-violation conditions (e.g., out-of-bounds indices, missing required values, exceeded limits) should include the entity's identifier, the actual offending value, and the valid range or configured limit so the message is immediately actionable without requiring source-code inspection — e.g., `Block ${id} width ${actual} exceeds configured column width ${limit}`.

When a GitHub Actions tool that has a dedicated config-validator workflow (e.g., `pr-labeler-config-validator.yml`) is replaced or removed, also delete the validator workflow — running validation for a config format that is no longer in use has no value and clutters CI.

When a helper function already closes over module-level state, prefer deriving dependent values internally rather than accepting pre-computed derivatives as explicit parameters. This keeps the function signature minimal and avoids inconsistencies between closure state and explicit arguments.

When creating a new package in this monorepo, audit its `devDependencies` and `scripts` for any `standard`-related entries (the linting tool the project previously used) and remove them; the project has migrated to `prettier` for formatting.

When adding or updating external links in the VitePress top bar component (`TopBar.vue`), ensure the URL includes UTM tracking parameters (e.g., `utm_source`, `utm_medium`, `utm_campaign`) so that traffic attribution to external sites can be measured in analytics.

Diagram renderers and layout functions must read runtime configuration from the diagram's config section via `configApi.getConfig().<diagramName>` or through `diagObj.db` accessor methods (e.g., `diagObj.db.getShowData()`), not by hardcoding values or reading from generic `conf`/`globalConfig` objects.

Place test files co-located with the module under test (e.g., `src/utils/subGraphTitleMargins.spec.ts` next to `src/utils/subGraphTitleMargins.ts`) rather than adding new tests to the shared `utils.spec.ts`, which is intentionally being split up. Name utility files after the module's domain/concern (e.g., `subGraphTitleMargins.ts`) rather than after a specific exported function.

Development scratch demos, backup files (e.g., `*-old.md`), generated temp files (e.g., Vite timestamp `.mjs` files), unused asset files, and work-in-progress files from unrelated features should NOT be committed. Use the `demos/dev` folder for ephemeral development demos; files checked into `demos/` should be durable, meaningful examples.

When adding a tool-setup step (e.g., `pnpm/action-setup`) to a GitHub Actions workflow, include an inline comment or note in the PR description explaining why it is required. In this project (which uses pnpm), `npx` commands that auto-detect lock files will try to invoke pnpm and fail if it is not installed in the runner; make this dependency explicit.
When adding a new demo page under `demos/`, register it with a link in `demos/index.html` so it appears in the demo index.

Do not add individual sub-type exports to `packages/parser/src/index.ts` for every AST node sub-property. Instead, export the `RecursiveAstOmit<T>` utility from the parser package and use it in consuming code (e.g., in diagram `types.ts`) to derive clean, non-`AstNode` types from the top-level exported AST type.

Prefix all diagram-specific rule names in Langium `.langium` files with the diagram identifier (e.g., `PacketBlock` not `Block`) to prevent naming collisions across diagram grammars and with Langium built-in AST node types.

In a diagram's `styles.ts`: (a) type the exported styles function as `DiagramStylesProvider` (from `../../diagram-api/types.js`); (b) define a named default style-options constant (e.g., `defaultPacketStyleOptions`); and (c) merge caller-supplied options with that constant using `cleanAndMerge` rather than hard-coding defaults inline.

Place all AST-to-DB population logic (walking the parsed AST and calling DB mutation methods) in the diagram's `parser.ts`, not in `db.ts`. The `db.ts` module should expose only mutation and query methods; the parser drives state population.

Place all type and interface definitions for a diagram module—data structures, domain types, and style option interfaces—in the diagram's `types.ts` file. Do not define them inline in `db.ts` or `styles.ts`.

Diagram unit test files (`*.spec.ts`) must include explicit test cases for diagram metadata fields (`getDiagramTitle`, `getAccTitle`, `getAccDescription`); do not delegate metadata coverage solely to Cypress e2e tests.

In GitHub Actions workflows that use `actions/setup-node`, always specify the Node.js version via `node-version-file:` pointing to the project's canonical version file (e.g., `node-version-file: '.node-version'`, or `node-version-file: 'package.json'` if a `volta.node` field is present) rather than hardcoding a version string inline. This keeps all workflows in sync with the project's intended Node version.

Ensure variable, parameter, and class field names accurately describe their purpose — use descriptive, semantically meaningful names instead of single-letter or terse abbreviations (e.g., `siblingWidth`/`siblingHeight` instead of `w`/`h`, `today` instead of `dt`, `latestEndingTask` instead of abbreviated alternatives, `radius` not `radious`, `count` not `cnt`); avoid shadowing outer-scope variable names with same-named inner-scope variables. Parameters that receive a delimited string representing multiple values (e.g., comma-separated CSS styles) should be named in the plural (e.g., `styles` rather than `style`). Do not use the underscore prefix (`_name`) on parameters that are actually read inside the function body. When adding public-facing methods, ensure the function name precisely describes what it returns or does (e.g., prefer `getRegisteredDiagramIDs` over `getRegisteredDiagramsMetadata` when only IDs are returned). When lifting module-level variables into class fields, declare an explicit access modifier (`private`, `protected`, or `public`) on every field.

For class-based diagram DB modules (preferred for new diagram types), manage all mutable state as direct class instance properties (e.g., `private nodes: Node[] = []`); the class itself is the state container and `ImperativeState` is not needed. For functional-export DB modules, use the `const db = { ... } as const satisfies DiagramDB` export pattern so that TypeScript infers the DB type automatically (e.g., `export type BlockDB = typeof db & DiagramDB`), eliminating the need for manually written parallel type declarations.
When adding a `styles.ts` file for a new diagram type, add a corresponding test case in `packages/mermaid/src/styles.spec.ts` to verify the style function.

When adding a new diagram config section to `config.schema.yaml`, do not redeclare defaults (e.g., `useMaxWidth`) that are already defined and inherited from `BaseDiagramConfig`; only add properties specific to the new diagram.

Documentation for a diagram type must cover all supported syntax features with usage examples, including non-obvious options (e.g., `columns auto`, `space:N`, `%%` comments); remove duplicate sections. Keep diagram code examples consistent with surrounding prose descriptions — if the text says a feature behaves a certain way, the example must demonstrate that behavior.

When duplicating a function that already exists in another diagram module, add a `// TODO:` or `@privateRemarks TODO:` comment noting the duplication and the intended consolidation point to prevent silent drift between the copies.

Access diagram config default values consistently across the codebase. Diagrams should import `defaultConfig` from `defaultConfig.ts` as an explicit fallback (following the pattern in `pieDb.ts`) rather than ad-hoc optional-chaining + nullish-coalescing scattered throughout rendering and DB modules. Avoid introducing helper types that claim to represent 'defaults' but actually return the current (possibly user-overridden) configuration, as these names are misleading.

Avoid patching third-party dependencies directly in the repository (e.g., via `pnpm patchedDependencies`). When a dependency lacks a necessary feature (such as a missing ESM `exports` field), raise an upstream PR first. If a temporary in-repo patch is unavoidable, document clearly why native support is absent and link to the open upstream issue or PR.

When a community platform link (e.g., Slack, Discord) is replaced in documentation, update all surrounding body prose that still names the old platform — not just the hyperlink anchor text and URL. Use the project's officially maintained canonical invite URL rather than generating a new ad-hoc invite.

When adding a Langium parser for a new diagram type under `packages/parser/src/language/`, follow the established two-tier abstraction pattern: create a `<Diagram>TokenBuilder` that extends `AbstractMermaidTokenBuilder` (passing diagram-specific keywords to `super()`) and a `<Diagram>ValueConverter` that extends `AbstractMermaidValueConverter`. Never duplicate keyword-restriction logic across token builders. Use `CommonTokenBuilder` / `CommonValueConverter` only for diagram parsers that require no specialization. Abstract base classes in this layer carry an `Abstract` prefix (e.g., `AbstractMermaidTokenBuilder`); shared concrete implementations carry a `Common` prefix (e.g., `CommonTokenBuilder`).

When importing the mermaid parser within `packages/mermaid/src/`, use the published package alias `mermaid-parser` as the module specifier (e.g., `import { parse } from 'mermaid-parser'`) rather than the scoped name `@mermaid-js/parser`.

In `populate*Db` helper functions in `packages/mermaid/src/diagrams/`, name the database parameter `db` to match the local import identifier and stay consistent with how `populateDb`-style functions are written across other diagram types in the project.

Shared rendering helpers that must work across multiple diagram types — such as font-icon substitution, math typesetting, or other text-transformation utilities — should be implemented in `packages/mermaid/src/diagrams/common/common.ts` rather than in individual diagram renderer files, so the capability is uniformly available to every diagram type without duplication.

When deprecating a function in JSDoc, always link to the replacement using `{@link ReplacementFunction}` syntax inside the `@deprecated` tag (e.g., `/** @deprecated Use {@link getBoundaries} instead */`), so IDEs and documentation tools can resolve the reference.

When updating the CSpell configuration, ensure the top-level `language` setting includes both `en-US` and `en-GB` (e.g., `language: en-US,en-GB`) so that both American and British English spellings are accepted project-wide without requiring per-file `cspell:locale` overrides.

When adding a new entry to the community integrations list in `packages/mermaid/src/docs/ecosystem/integrations-community.md`, insert it in alphabetical order within its respective category section (e.g., 'Content Management Systems', 'Blogging frameworks', etc.).

Within a function that normalizes a string parameter at the top (e.g., `str = str.trim()`), do not call the same normalization method on that variable again in subsequent expressions within the same function body; the variable is already in its normalized form.

When adding tests for new functionality in an existing test file, add new standalone test cases rather than modifying the content of existing ones. Existing test cases may intentionally exercise specific edge cases — such as inconsistent whitespace, unusual formatting, or deliberately invalid input — and altering or removing them silently drops that coverage.

When reviewing a newly added `package.json` dependency, do not request that the author manually bump its version to the latest release; this project uses Renovate Bot to keep dependency versions up to date automatically.

When a PR mixes a non-visual bug fix with a visual theme-variable change, split them into separate PRs. In this project, any change that alters rendered output triggers visual regression tests that require a mermaid-js admin to approve the merge; non-visual changes (e.g., fixing a DOM attribute bug, adding an identifier attribute) can be merged without that gate.

When adding a new `###` section to `packages/mermaid/src/docs/ecosystem/integrations-community.md`, place list items directly under the heading without an introductory prose description paragraph — the heading alone is sufficient to label the category. Only include a short expansion line when the heading is an abbreviation that would be unclear on its own (e.g., 'CRM/ERP').

A bugfix that changes rendered output for users who had previously configured specific settings — even if correcting incorrect behavior — should be released as a MINOR semver bump, not a PATCH, because it constitutes a visible behavior change for existing users. When a refactoring changes a publicly exported API shape (e.g., replacing an exported singleton object with a class export), classify the changeset as `major` rather than `patch` if it is breaking for downstream consumers.

When adding new test cases covering a new variant of an existing feature, group them in a new nested `describe` block rather than appending to or altering existing test cases; this keeps the snapshot namespace stable and makes the test hierarchy self-documenting.

When typing a property or parameter that is a single-field wrapper object (e.g., `{ actor: string }`), evaluate whether the primitive type can be used directly; accept the wrapper only when the shape genuinely needs to vary or flattening would cascade changes to the parser layer.

When a function parameter is an object that callers may legitimately omit, model it as a default empty-object parameter with optional fields (e.g., `opts: { text?: string; wrap?: boolean } = {}`) rather than marking the entire parameter optional (`opts?:`); this removes the need to null-check the object reference throughout the function body.

In jison diagram parsers, accept style definitions as a single raw string token rather than parsing individual style properties within grammar rules; delegate style string parsing and validation to the JavaScript DB layer, following the pattern in `packages/mermaid/src/diagrams/flowchart/parser/flow.jison`.
Use TypeScript `interface extends` and `Pick<>` to compose new interfaces from existing base types rather than redeclaring fields that already exist in those types.

When fixing a broken or changed URL in documentation, search the entire docs tree — both `packages/mermaid/src/docs/` and the generated `docs/` directory — for every occurrence of the old URL and update them all consistently in the same MR.

When listing plugins or integrations in documentation, use the plugin's full official product name as link text (e.g., 'Mermaid Chart GPT for ChatGPT') rather than only the host platform name, so entries unambiguously identify the specific product.

In `sequenceRenderer.ts`, all coordinate and position adjustments (e.g., `startx`/`stopx` offsets per arrow type) must be computed inside `buildMessageModel`, which owns layout calculations. The `drawMessage` function must only render from the dimensions it receives; do not add position-offset or geometry-correction logic inside the drawing path.

Do not add apparent source-code typos (e.g., `egdes` for `edges`, `affedcting` for `affecting`) to `.cspell/misc-terms.txt` as a workaround to silence spell-check errors. Fix the typo in the source instead. Reserve `.cspell/misc-terms.txt` for legitimate project-specific terms that are not in standard dictionaries (e.g., library names, domain vocabulary, or config-key names like `handdrawnSeed`).

When refactoring for cleanliness, avoid inlining or eliminating named intermediate variables that hold the result of a non-trivial call or computation. A named binding (e.g., `const direction = getDirection()`) makes the value inspectable at a breakpoint; the debuggability benefit outweighs the cosmetic gain of inlining the call at its use site.

In focused cleanup or chore PRs, do not remove code or functionality that is still under active investigation or that is explicitly planned for removal in a subsequent, larger coordinated PR. Confirm with the team that the code is safe to drop before including the removal; otherwise defer it to the appropriate milestone PR.

When a component is removed from all its usage sites (e.g., unregistered from VitePress layout slots in `packages/mermaid/src/docs/.vitepress/theme/index.ts`), check whether the component's source file should also be deleted to avoid accumulating dead code. If the file is intentionally retained for anticipated future use, document that intent with an inline comment in the component file or at the removal site.

All new configuration properties — including diagram rendering hints (such as `look`) and layout-engine options (such as ELK settings) — must be added to the MermaidConfig type as properly nested objects (e.g., `elk: { mergeEdges: true, nodePlacement: { strategy: 'SIMPLE' } }`) rather than as flat string-valued options or ad-hoc top-level properties on diagram DB objects; this maintains consistency with the existing nested MermaidConfig structure.

When calling db functions from the parser or visitor layer with multiple optional arguments, pass a named-property object rather than a positional array for clarity and resilience to parameter reordering.

When enabling pnpm via corepack in the Dockerfile, do not hardcode or independently specify a pnpm version. Use `corepack enable` (and optionally `corepack enable pnpm`) without an explicit version argument so that the active pnpm version is driven by the `packageManager` field in `package.json`, keeping Docker builds consistent with the rest of the toolchain.

New files added to `demos/` must match the HTML boilerplate conventions (DOCTYPE format, attribute quoting, meta tags, script structure) of existing demo files in that directory. When in doubt, copy the structure of a nearby demo file rather than starting from scratch.

In Langium grammar files (`.langium`), if you intentionally omit the import of the project's shared common grammar (which other diagram grammars conventionally import), add an inline comment explaining the reason — e.g., that the common grammar introduces ambiguity or parser conflicts with this grammar's own token/rule definitions.

In diagram documentation's 'Related Diagrams' or 'See Also' sections, every currently-supported Mermaid diagram type that is mentioned must include a relative hyperlink to its documentation page (e.g., `[Pie Charts](./pie.md)`). Diagram types that are not yet released may be mentioned in plain text without a link.

When adding new diagram examples to `packages/examples`, consider storing each diagram's code in a separate `.mmd` file (imported as a raw string, e.g., via Vite's `?raw` suffix) rather than as an inline TypeScript template literal. External `.mmd` files enable IDE syntax highlighting and Mermaid editor plugins for developers who maintain the examples.

Each `.changeset/*.md` file should cover changes for exactly one package. If an MR touches multiple packages with distinct user-facing changes, run `pnpm changeset` once per package so that each package's `CHANGELOG.md` receives only its own relevant entry.

Do not add a changeset file for changes that only affect devDependencies; in this project's changesets workflow, changeset entries are only needed when the published package output, public API, or runtime behavior changes.

In `package.json`, prefer semver range specifiers (e.g., `^3.6.0`) over bare exact pins (e.g., `3.6.0`) unless there is an explicit, documented reason to lock a dependency to a precise version; an exact pin with no explanation signals that future patch/minor upgrades are unsafe, which may not be intentional.

In class-based diagram DB modules, do not initialize or reset state in the constructor. The Mermaid `Diagram` class automatically calls `db.clear?.()` before each parse cycle, so all state initialization and reset logic belongs only in the `clear()` method.

In VitePress documentation components, preserve fully-qualified `href` URLs on all anchor and CTA elements even when a Vue event handler overrides click behavior — search engine crawlers depend on the `href` attribute being present in server-rendered HTML for SEO indexing.

When writing tests with `jsdomIt` (the project's JSDOM-backed test helper in `packages/mermaid/src/tests/util.ts`), always accept and use the environment parameters it provides by destructuring them in the callback signature (e.g., `({ svg })` or `({ body })`) rather than obtaining those references through other means inside the test body.

Keep changeset description text and PR descriptions synchronized with the actual implementation behavior: if the code logs a warning rather than throwing an error (or vice versa), the description must reflect that distinction accurately.
Performance Issue: When reviewing changes to build entry points in `.esbuild/util.cjs` (or any esbuild build configuration), verify that each new entry point is intentional and explicitly justified: each additional entry point produces a full separate bundle in `dist/`, potentially adding tens of megabytes to the output.

Avoid calling `getConfig()` multiple times within a single function, and do not re-declare or shadow a config object that is already available in scope (e.g., a module-level `gitGraphConfig` in `gitGraphRenderer.js`). Never call `getConfig()` inside recursive or shared helper functions where it would be re-invoked on every recursion. Internal rendering functions (e.g., in `packages/mermaid/src/rendering-util/` and `packages/mermaid/src/dagre-wrapper/`) must not call or import `getConfig` directly; instead, accept an explicit `config: MermaidConfig` parameter. Call `getConfig()` once at the top-level entry point and thread the resulting config object as an explicit parameter down to helpers and recursive calls. This prevents redundant work, avoids stale-config bugs, and supports the architectural goal of enabling parallel/async rendering.

When finding the maximum (or minimum) value in an array, use `Math.max(...array)` (O(n)) rather than sorting the array and popping the last element (O(n log n)). The former is also more readable and idiomatic.

Prefer `{ ...obj }` (shallow) or `assignWithDepth(target, source)` (deep) instead of `lodash.clone()` / `lodash.cloneDeep()` when copying objects, to avoid unnecessary bundle size from lodash imports. For merging or cloning config objects specifically, prefer `assignWithDepth` over `structuredClone`, as `structuredClone` is not universally supported across all target browser environments.

Heavy optional dependencies (e.g., KaTeX for math typesetting) should be dynamically imported (`await import(...)`) only when actually needed at runtime: gate the import on both the text containing the relevant syntax (e.g., a `$$…$$` delimiter check) AND the environment supporting the feature (e.g., `isMathMLSupported() || config.legacyMathML`). Importing at module load time unconditionally inflates the bundle for all users, even those who never use the feature.
Code Style: Proofread prose in JSDoc comments, documentation, log messages, thrown error strings, test fixtures, demo files, and diagram example code strings (including node labels, comments, and descriptions in `packages/examples/src/examples/*.ts`) for spelling, grammar, and terminological accuracy. These appear in production output, developer tooling, end-user tools like mermaid.live, or snapshot diffs, making errors harder to catch than code mistakes. In documentation under `packages/mermaid/src/docs/`, verify that descriptions match what the grammar actually supports (e.g., 'single word' vs 'single line' when describing quoting rules).
In GitHub Actions workflow YAML files, when a step needs to execute from a specific directory, use the `working-directory` step attribute rather than embedding a `cd` command inside the `run:` block.

In test files, template-literal diagram strings should not include a trailing newline before the closing backtick. The backtick should appear immediately after the last content line. When adding test cases, match the indentation style and closing-backtick placement used by the surrounding tests in the same file for readability and consistency.
TypeScript `interface` declarations should end with a trailing semicolon after the closing brace (`};`), for consistency with `type` alias declarations in the same file.

Do not leave commented-out code, dead code, unused variables, unused function parameters, unused imports, unused exported types/functions, or unresolved inline comments whose purpose is pending verification (e.g., 'check with X before removing') in a merge request. Delete all dead and unreferenced code (in both source and test files), and resolve pending-verification comments — either remove them or convert to proper TSDoc — before merging. When a renderer or module is fully superseded by a new implementation, delete the old file entirely (e.g., `flowRenderer-v2.js`). When migrating a diagram from a legacy parser (e.g., a `.jison` file) to a new Langium-based parser, delete the old parser file in the same PR. Git history preserves prior versions.

In jison grammar rule actions, prefer named semantic-value aliases (`$symbolName` or explicit label aliases via `symbol[alias]` syntax) over positional `$1`/`$2` references. Named aliases prevent off-by-one errors when alternatives are reordered or new tokens are inserted, and make the rule body self-documenting.

When flowchart parser tests exercise the same assertion body across multiple shapes, edge types, or token categories, use `it.each` or a plain JS array iteration (`forEach`/`map` over a data-table) rather than duplicating the test body for each case. This reduces file size, makes coverage intent explicit, and makes adding new cases trivial.

When adding or reordering numbered step headings (e.g., `#### N. Title`) in documentation, verify that step numbers are strictly sequential with no duplicates — each new section must use the next unused number.
In TypeScript files, use type-only import declarations (`import type { Foo } from '...'`) rather than inline type qualifiers inside a mixed import list (`import { type Foo } from '...'`).

In jison lexers, whitespace should be ignored in the INITIAL state (e.g., a rule that consumes `\s+` with no action) rather than returned as tokens and threaded through grammar rules; only include whitespace tokens in states where they carry semantic meaning.
Non-terminal names in jison grammars should not be prefixed with 'parse' (the whole file is a parser); ensure names are correctly spelled (e.g., `commaSeparated` not `commaSeprate`).

When the same regex pattern applies across multiple jison lexer states, combine the states in a single rule using a comma-separated state list (e.g., `<state1,state2>regexp { ... }`) rather than duplicating the rule once per state.

Extract unexplained numeric literals (magic numbers) in rendering, parser, and layout code into named constants with descriptive names (e.g., `const BAR_WIDTH_TO_TICK_WIDTH_RATIO = 0.7`, `const MAX_PACKET_SIZE = 10_000`) at the top of the relevant scope, and replace every hard-coded occurrence with those constants. For values that should be user-configurable, expose them as named properties in the diagram's default config object rather than hardcoding.
